New Zealand have put up a formidable total after being asked to bat first by Shreyas Iyer. The average first-innings score at this venue is 276, while teams batting first in wins have posted 314 on an average, making this a challenging target for the opposition. Will Young made the most of two reprieves in the second over, producing a rollicking knock to register his fifth ODI century. At the other end, Tim Seifert provided an aggressive start, with the opening pair laying a solid foundation through a valuable partnership. The middle order struggled to make an impact, with Finn Allen the only exception. Mitchell Santner, Clarke and Jamieson chipped in with valuable contributions down the order, providing the late impetus New Zealand needed to push past the 330-run mark. With the ball, Axar Patel was India's standout performer, picking up a couple of wickets while maintaining excellent control and keeping the scoring rate in check. Auqib Nabi was impressive with the ball as well, creating several opportunities and keeping the batters under pressure. However, his efforts weren't fully rewarded, with a number of dropped catches preventing him from adding more wickets to his tally. Can India chase it down and take an unassailable lead of 3-0 in this series? Join us back in 30 minutes for all the answers..

[125 runs, highest ODI score and fifth ODI century, your feelings on the knock] A little bit of relief, firstly, but no, it's been amazing to spend some time in the middle. Obviously a little bit of fortune early in my innings, but I managed to stick at it and put a decent score together with a few partnerships in the middle. [Reaction to two consecutive dropped catches] Well, the first one, obviously a little bit disappointed, but at the same time relieved. The second one, you just got to laugh it off. . [Adjusting his batting approach after the dropped catches] Yeah, I did actually notice that I was a little bit stuck on the crease after that, those two drops. I decided to walk at them and get my weight through the ball a bit more, and that seemed to work in my favour.

[Enjoyment during the innings and partnerships] I try to enjoy myself the whole time. Obviously, having Seifert at the other end in the opening partnership was brilliant. He played really well, and I think it was just a story of small partnerships throughout the innings, which got us to that 333. When Finn came to the middle, he talked about enjoying it and playing with a smile on his face, so that was great to see too. [Assessment of the total and expectations for the second innings] Yeah, I think at a certain stage in the innings we would have liked a little bit more, but we did keep losing wickets. So to scrap through to 333 I think is a decent score. Obviously it might be a little bit easier chasing, but I think stats say that 314 is the average first innings winning score. So hopefully that's enough. Early wickets, feel like demons, hopefully it is.

"It still looks absolutely magnificent out here. 333, and I kind of feel that I0$. A little roll is going up and down at the moment, just pushing back any little indentations that have been made, but there just isn't any. I can't see anything where the ball's pitched, taken up any of the little scuffs or taken any grass out of the surface at all. It still feels very hard. I thought it was a little bit softer earlier, but it's really hardened up nicely underneath the sun. As I say, I can't see any reason why you wouldn't be pretty happy chasing that sort of score at the moment from an Indian point of view. We did see, though, early on the ball nip around just a little bit. New Zealand will be hoping that that has not changed. Auqib Nabi got the ball to nip away a few times and picked up the outside edge of Will Young's bat. India just couldn't hold their catches. That's going to be the key for New Zealand - holding the catches if the chances come early on, they might be able to defend it."

After the post-match handshakes, Matt Henry and Kohli walk up the stairs having a chat. Would be nice to be a fly on the wall, hearing what they are talking. The former the star with a six-fer and he practically ended this game after the first over of the innings. He got Rohit, Kohli and Shreyas out to leave India tottering at 0/3. Soon it became 9/4 and should've been 9/5 but Nick Kelly dropped a sitter to allow Axar a reprieve. Axar went after a little stand and then Henry came back to get Ishan first ball of his 2nd spell. The end came soon after.  The conditions didn't change much in the chase but the incredible Henry was on fire and he was well backed up by the rest of his mates. Lots of Indians in the crowd and they are now walking off the Bay Oval, as the game ends way too early for their liking. Stay tuned for the post-match stuff....
